newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel weakens, low sulphur stable.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel weakens, low sulphur stable.

text.p: High sulphur fuel prices drifted lower on Monday while the low sulphur market was becalmed in a typically quiet start to the week.
High sulphur barges started the day trading at $82 fob ARA, off $2, before picking up in stages to $83.50. Bunker interest was reported as moderate.
The high sulphur cargo market lost some of Friday's gains, with offers heard around $83 and $84 cif but no buyer interest reported at that price.

High sulphur gained $4 on Friday on the back of a cargo trade from Coryton, U.K., to a German purchaser with a reported requirement in Portugal. It traded at a healthy $80 fob, though was said to be good quality.
A trader was heard to be offering a high sulphur cargo at $84 cif NWE but was said to be hard to pin down.
The low sulphur market was quiet, with prices notionally stable at $90.50 fob, showing little reaction to Friday's late fall in the value of crude or Monday's recovery in the screen price.
A 5,000 tonne packet of poor quality material was heard traded on Friday at $89.
